newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Mark, yen vols off highs, stg vols jump.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Mark, yen vols off highs, stg vols jump.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark and dollar/yen options drifted off their highs in the U.S. as spot slid from their peaks just short of key levels, traders said.
Sterling volatilities, on the other hand, remained firm as the spot cable flirted with the $1.60 level after plunging overnight toward $1.59 from mid-$1.62 levels.
"It's caught the market by surprise, coming ahead of the possible rate hike decision tomorrow," said Soma Rao, first vice president and options sales manager at Smith Barney.
He was referring to the Bank of England's monetary policy committee meeting ending Thursday.

Expectation of tighter credit had bolstered sterling to mid-July highs just below $1.70, but the pound's very strength as well as some spotty economic figures recently has raised doubts that there would be another rate rise this week.
Implied volatility for one-month cable shot up to around 10.3/10.6 percent from 8.8/9.1 late on Tuesday.
"I think the risk is that either the market does not get the rate hike that it's looking for or if you do get a rate hike, it could be the last for a while," Rao said.
"There's still good demand in the longer maturities, and that's why the curve has been positively sloped," she said. "The shorter dates are spot-sensitive and driven by day-to-day factors."
She added that a spot rally above 120 yen and 1.90 marks would likely pull out a lot of stop-loss buying in spot and further buoy volatilities.
Traders said a lot of short option positions were likely to have piled up in strike prices above 120 yen and 1.90 marks, also keeping the market nervous.

Dollar/mark sagged below 1.88 marks in the U.S. after leaping to 1.8913, the highest level in nearly eight years, while dollar/yen slipped below 119 yen after taking out Tuesday's high and edging closer to the 120-yen.
One-month dollar/mark stood at 11.2/11.5 percent at U.S. midsession after rising as high as 12.0/12.3 percent earlier from 11.0/11.2 late on Tuesday.
One-month dollar/yen stood at 12.0/12.2 percent after surging to 12.4/12.6 from Tuesday's 11.9/12.1.
The movement was similar across the maturity curve in both currency pairs, although somewhat less choppy in the back end.
